extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers looking for biographical information about the actress Jean Smart
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography page for actress Jean Smart summarizing her life, career, roles, awards, and critical reception, with incidental evaluative language about her comedic and dramatic performing qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Smart has the voice and the timing to play a stern matriarch"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by critics to explain suitability for certain roles; implies that vocal quality and comedic/dramatic timing are key evaluative dimensions for her performances (particularly as a tough, authoritative character).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic delivery / monologue performance
rubrics_metrics.description: "delivering jokes like the pro comic she plays on Hacks"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates an actor's ability to perform standup-style material and monologues convincingly — includes pacing, punchline delivery, stage presence, and ability to carry a comedic monologue (also evidenced by her hosting SNL and monologue performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic flair in performing routines
rubrics_metrics.description: "performing Deborah's vaguely hokey routines with a naturalistic flair as if she was born to it"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how naturally and believably an actor performs intentionally awkward or stylized comedic material; a 'naturalistic flair' makes routines feel authentic rather than staged or forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen/stage presence (ability to command attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: "whenever she's onscreen in Mare of Easttown, she wrenches away the spotlight like she's grabbing a juice box."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for evaluating how much an actor dominates a scene or captures audience attention — includes charisma, energy, and capacity to draw focus even in ensemble settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit between actor and role (role-authenticity)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I don't know if the role of Deborah Vance was written for Smart, but she certainly makes it seem like it was..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses how convincingly an actor inhabits a part such that the performance feels tailor-made; includes alignment of actor's persona/skills with the character's demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility across genres and media
rubrics_metrics.description: "Her work includes both comedy and drama" and her credits span stage, television, film, and voice acting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates range — ability to perform in multiple genres (comedic and dramatic) and across different media (stage, screen, voice) as evidence of professional breadth and adaptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional depth / compelling characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics described her Watchmen performance as "compelling" and called her portrayal a "cynical, heroically-damaged middle-aged version" of the character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge the actor's capacity to convey complex inner life and emotional nuance, especially in dramatic or morally ambiguous roles.
